Kaitlyn and Eli were planning  
to go to the beach.
We use words like chance, most likely,  
probably, unlikely and certain in our  
everyday conversations. These words  
all have meaning in the study of  
chance and probability. 
Probability is a way of describing the  
chance of something happening.
An event that will not happen has a probability of zero (0).
An event that will definitely occur has a probability of 1.
These are the two end points of the probability line.

The possible outcomes are the different results (or events) that can happen.
Most probability questions involve random events.

16 – Achieve! Maths – Data, statistics and drawing graphs 
 
© Paul Steenson and Blake Education 2013
Data is the information collected from a  
survey or census. There are two types of data:
•  Numerical data consists of numbers.  
It is collected by counting or measuring.  
For example: the number of students in  
each class can be counted; the heights 
of students in a class can be measured. 
Numerical data is often displayed in a 
frequency histogram.
•  Categorical data consists of words or letters. For example: the colour of  
each student’s hair may be brown, black, blonde or red; your grade in a  
class test may be A, B, C, D or E. Categorical data is often displayed in  
a picture graph or a column graph.
1 
State whether the following data is Numerical (N) or Categorical (C).
2.1 Types of data

each month

in a bag   
Numerical data can be described as discrete or continuous.
•  Discrete data is obtained by counting.  
For example, the number of children in a family.
•  Continuous data is obtained by measuring. The results are often rounded off  
to a required accuracy. For example, the length of telephone calls.

Achieve! Maths – Data, statistics and drawing graphs – 17
Data can be obtained from many sources. It is 
available on the internet and in the media. Often 
you need to conduct a survey or a census to obtain 
the information you need.
A census is taken when you ask everyone to provide 
the information. Every five years, the Australian 
Bureau of Statistics conducts a national census. 
Information is collected from every member of the 
community.
It is not easy to conduct a census every time you 
need data. A survey is conducted using a sample 
from the population. The size of the sample and how 
it is selected can affect the accuracy of the results. 
There are a number of ways to obtain a sample.
•  Random sampling: For example, everyone’s name is placed in a hat.  
The names of 20 people are selected without looking.
•  Systematic sampling: For example, every fifth name on an alphabetical list 
is selected.
• Stratified sampling: For example, equal numbers of girls and boys are selected.

Suzanne conducted a survey 
of the students in her class. 
She asked each student how 
many children were in their 
family. She recorded the 
following data:
When you conduct a survey 
you can collect a lot of 
data. You need a way to 
organise and display the 
information so that it is 
easily understood.
One way to organise data is to use a frequency table and tally marks.
To complete a frequency table:
Step 1 
 List all the different scores or results in the first column.  
When you are using numerical data, first circle the smallest and largest 
scores in the data. Then, list the different scores in ascending order 
(smallest to largest). 
Step 2 
 Work across each row in the data, and put a tally mark (a stroke) for each 
score. Every fifth stroke beside a score is made diagonally.
Step 3 
 Count up the number of tally marks for each score. Write these numbers 
in the frequency column.
Step 4 
 Find the total of the frequency column. Check that this is equal to the 
number of scores in the original data.
Step 5 
Write a heading (or title) for your table.

Rochelle plays cricket with her school team. Her recent batting scores were  
10, 25, 17 and 40 runs. The coach wanted to calculate her average score.
The term average is used in many situations. For example, batting averages  
in cricket or the average monthly rainfall.
The mean is the mathematical term for the average of a set of scores. 
To calculate the mean we add all the scores and then  
divide the sum by the number of scores.
Mean = the sum of the scores ÷ the number of scores
Calculate the mean of 10, 25, 17 and 40.
The sum of the scores = 10 + 25 + 17 + 40 = 92
The number of scores = 4
Mean = the sum of the scores ÷ the number of scores
 
= 92 ÷ 4 = 23
Rochelle’s average batting score was 23 runs.

The mean, median and mode are all used  
to describe the middle of a set of scores.  
This is sometimes called the central tendency.
Each of these terms can be used to answer  
a certain type of question.
•  The mean is the mathematical term for  
the average of a set of scores. For example,  
the average family in Woodport has 2.4 children.
•  The median is the middle score after the scores are arranged in order from 
smallest to largest. Half the scores are smaller than the median. The other half are 
larger than the median. For example, the middle height of the students in a class. 
•  The mode is the score that occurs most often. It is the score with the highest 
frequency. For example, the most popular television actor and the most common 
dress size.

Sue is the goal shooter in her netball team. This dot plot shows the number of 
goals she scored in the last 14 matches.
A dot plot is like a column graph.  
It is used for small sets of  
numerical data.
The scores are equally spaced  
along a horizontal number line.  
The dots should be equally  
spaced vertically.  
Each dot represents one result.  
So, Sue scored 6 goals in 2 matches.
A dot plot makes it easy to see where the scores are clustered together.  
It is also easy to see gaps in the data.

Achieve! Maths – Decimals and fractions – 7
The number system we use today was devised by the Hindu people who lived in 
the area of modern India. It was taken to Europe by Arab traders. 
Our number system uses ten symbols called digits: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 0. 
The position of each digit determines its place value in a numeral.
For example, 8 736 means 8 thousands, 7 hundreds, 3 tens and 6 units.

Achieve! Maths – Decimals and fractions – 15
Josie’s calculator showed an answer as:
The question required an answer to the nearest whole number. 
When using decimals, we often have more digits after  
the decimal point than we need. This may happen  
after completing a multiplication or division. 
If this does happen, we round off to the number of 
decimal places that we need and leave out the  
following digits. Looking at a number line or  
the scale on your ruler can make this easier.
 
Rule for rounding a decimal
 
 
1  Cut the numeral at the required place.
 
 
2  Look at the next digit to the right of the cut.
 
 
3   If this next digit is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4, leave the previous digit unchanged. 
(This is called rounding down.)
 
 
     If this next digit is 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9, add 1 to the previous digit.  
(This is called rounding up.)

Achieve! Maths – Decimals and fractions – 41
Fractions allow us to show how whole numbers are broken into parts.  
For example, games of water polo, football, basketball and many other  
sports are played in halves or quarters. 
A fraction indicates part of a whole number or quantity.   
The diagram shows how a rectangular sheet of paper  
has been folded to form three equal parts.
The shaded part is one-third ( 1 
3 ) of the whole sheet of paper.
The sheet of paper is folded again to form six equal parts.  
Five parts have been shaded. 
Five-sixths ( 5 
6 ) of the rectangle is shaded.
Every fraction has a numerator and a denominator.
•  The numerator is the top number.  
It indicates the number of shaded parts.
•  The denominator is the bottom number.  
It indicates the total number of equal parts. 
Answer questions 1 to 10 in your workbook.
For each diagram, write down:
a the number of equal parts (the denominator)
b the number of shaded parts (the numerator)
c the fraction shaded.

24 – Achieve! Maths – Graphs, number patterns and algebra  
© Paul Steenson and Blake Education 2010
A prime number has only two factors – itself and 1.
A number with more than two factors is called a composite number.
To find all the prime numbers less than 120, use the number grid on the next page 
and follow these steps carefully.
1 
Cross out 1. It is not a prime number. It does not have two factors.
2 Put a circle around 2. It is a prime number.
3 Cross out all the other even numbers. (The last digit will be 2, 4, 6, 8 or 0.) 
These are the multiples of 2. They are not prime numbers.
4 Put a circle around 3. It is the next prime number.
5 Cross out all the multiples of 3.  
They have more than two factors. They are not prime numbers.
6 Put a circle around 5. It is the next number not crossed out.  
It is the next prime number.
7 Cross out all the other multiples of 5. (The last digit will be 5 or 0.)
8 Put a circle around the next number  
not crossed out. It is 7.  
7 is the next prime number.
9 Cross out all the multiples of 7.
10 Put a circle around the next number  
not crossed out. It is 11.  
11 is the next prime number.
12 Cross out all the multiples of 11.
13 What is the next number not crossed out?            
 
This is the next prime number. Cross out any of its multiples that remain.
14 Check that the remaining numbers are prime and circle them.
15 List all the prime numbers less than 120. (All the numbers you have circled.) 
You should have 30 numbers.

2.4 Divisibility and factors
A factor is a number that exactly divides into another number.
One way to find the factors of a number without doing the actual division 
is to use the tests for divisibility.
Some simple tests for divisibility are listed below.
1 
Apply the sum of the digits test and circle the numbers which are divisible by 3.
 
75     89      137     249     376     438     516     754     1 625     8 229
2 Apply the last two digits test and circle the numbers which are divisible by 4.
 
116     234     348     552     747     1 082     1 496     2 002     3 116     4 614
3 Circle the numbers that are divisible by 5.
 
53     65     90     256     370     765     1 523     1 395     2 630     5 502
4 Circle the numbers that are divisible by 6.
 
84     96     124     369     636     1 266     1 323     2 351     5 610     7 398
5 Circle the numbers that are divisible by 9.
 
129     198     252     619     747     1 381     2 106     3 519     7 435     9 378
Unit 2: Number patterns
A number is:
• 
 divisible by 2 if the last 
digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8  
(i.e. an even number)
• 
 divisible by 3 if the sum of 
its digits is divisible by 3
• 
 divisible by 4 if the last 
two digits form a number  
that is divisible by 4
• 
 divisible by 5 if the last 
digit is 5 or 0
• 
 divisible by 6 if it is 
divisible by both 2 and 3 
(i.e. it is an even number 
and the sum of the digits is 
divisible by 3)
• 
 divisible by 8 if the last 
three digits form a number 
that is divisible by 8
• 
 divisible by 9 if the sum of 
the digits is divisible by 9
•

© Paul Steenson and Blake Education 2013
1 
At midday the temperature at Perisher Valley was 5°C.  
The temperature dropped 2°C every hour. 
 
What was the temperature at 6 pm?                                
2 In a game of indoor cricket, a team loses 5 runs off their score each time  
they lose a wicket. Sean’s team scored 123 runs, but lost 7 wickets. 
 
What is their final score?                                
3. The temperature was –2°C at 6 am yesterday morning.  
It rose by 7°C during the morning, and dropped 10°C during the afternoon.
 
What was the temperature at 6 pm?                                
4 The average temperature in January  
at Alice Springs was 29°C.  
At Beijing (China), the average  
temperature during January was –5°C.
 
What is the difference between  
these temperatures?
 
                               
5 Brendan had a debit balance of $463 in his credit card account at the 
beginning of the month. He owed $463. He made a payment of $260.  
Brendan then made purchases costing $47, $163, $85 and $124.
 
What is the new balance on his account?                                
6 Anita is scuba diving 70 metres below sea level.  
The water is 165 metres deep.  
A helicopter flying directly above Anita  
reports it is 150 metres above sea level.
a How far is Anita above the ocean floor?
 
                                
b How far is the helicopter above the  
ocean floor?
 
                               
c What is the vertical distance between Anita and the helicopter?

Achieve! Maths – Integers and the number plane – 33
A number plane is a grid using two 
number lines, called axes. 
One number line is drawn horizontal, 
across the page. It is called the x-axis. 
The second number line is drawn vertically, 
at right angles to the x-axis. The vertical 
axis is called the y-axis.
Any position on the grid can be named 
using an ordered pair of numbers. These 
numbers are called the co-ordinates of  
the point.
The two axes meet at the origin.  
It is the point (0, 0). It is always labelled O.
To locate a point, start at the origin.
The first number tells how far  
to move across, along the x-axis. 
The second number then tells you  
how far to move up.

The amount of liquid or gas that a container  
can hold is called the capacity of the container.
The basic unit used to measure capacity is

Unit 5: Time
Eastern Standard Time (Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania)  
is 30 minutes ahead of Central Standard Time.  
It is 30 minutes earlier in Adelaide than Brisbane.

It is 2 hours earlier in Perth than Brisbane.

4.5 Line symmetry
Many designs and buildings are symmetrical.  
They look well balanced and attractive to us. 
There are many examples of symmetry in nature,  
including beetles and butterflies. 
A plane shape has line symmetry if it can be folded  
along a line or reflected in a mirror so that the two halves  
match exactly. The line of the fold is called an axis of symmetry.
Some shapes have more than one axis of symmetry. For example, a rectangle 
can be folded in half 2 ways, as you can see in the diagram on the left below.
We use dotted lines to show each axis of symmetry.
However, if you try folding a 
rectangle along its diagonal, 
the two halves do not match 
exactly. This is not an axis of 
symmetry.

© Paul Steenson and Blake Education 2010
The size of an angle is the amount of turning between two lines  
which meet at a point. Angles are measured in degrees, using a protractor.
This angle measures 60°.  
Most protractors have two scales: a clockwise scale (left to right) and an 
anticlockwise scale (right to left). 
When you use a protractor, make sure that the centre point is at the vertex of 
the angle. The base line should be along one of the arms of the angle.
In each diagram below, a protractor has been placed over an angle.  
Read the scale on the protractor to find the size of each angle.

5.6 Using compasses
Compasses are very handy instruments.  
They can be used to draw circles or arcs.  
They are used in many geometric constructions.
Technical tips 
 
 
 
 
 
 
•  Line up the metal point and the tip of your  
pencil before using the compasses.
•  Be sure the legs of your compasses are securely 
positioned before you start to draw.
•  Place something between the sheet of paper and  
the desk, so that the metal tip does not slide.
•  Use the scale on your ruler to open the compasses  
to the correct radius.
•  When you are drawing a circle or an arc, hold your 
compasses by the top handle, not by the two legs. 
Complete the following constructions in your workbook.
1 
Use a pair of compasses to draw 3 circles.
a radius 5 cm 
 
b radius 8 cm 
 
c radius 65 mm
2 Use a pair of compasses and the same centre  
to draw 3 circles with radius:
a 4 cm. 
b 6 cm. 
c 7 cm.
These are called concentric circles  
because they have the same centre.
3 Refer to the diagram at the right to help you  
complete the following steps.
a Construct a circle with radius 45 mm. 
b Draw a diameter AB.  
(A diameter is a line drawn from one side of a 
circle to the other, passing through the centre.)
c Use a set square to draw a second diameter CD, perpendicular to AB.
d Join the points A, C, B and D.

64 – Achieve! Maths – Percentages, ratio and plane shapes  
© Paul Steenson and Blake Education 2010
A polygon is a plane shape bounded by straight sides,  
which do not cross over.
A regular polygon has equal sides and equal angles.
A circle is often used as the base for constructing a 
regular polygon. You can always draw a circle through 
the vertices of a regular polygon. 
You need a pair of compasses, a protractor and a ruler 
for the constructions on this activity sheet.
1 
Follow the steps below to construct a  
regular hexagon (6 sides) in your workbook. 
Step 1: Use a pair of compasses to construct 
a circle with radius 5 cm. (Alternatively, 
you could trace around a 360° protractor.)
Step 2: Mark the centre of your circle  
and label it point O.
Step 3: Draw a radius OA.
Step 4: Use your protractor to construct  
an angle BOA measuring 60°.
Step 5: Now construct an angle COB also 
measuring 60°. Then repeat this process 
to divide the circle into 6 sectors, each 
containing an angle of 60°.
Step 6: Join the points A, B, C, D, E and F  
to form a regular hexagon.
2 Repeat the steps in question 1 but 
use an angle of 45° instead of 60° to 
construct a regular octagon (8 sides).
